title: Ursa Coffee — 1km Competitor Census, Miraflores

studyArea.anchor: Ursa Coffee Roasters — Alcanfores 183, Miraflores, Lima 15074
studyArea.rationale: 1km is the practical walk-up catchment for an espresso-bar/café in a dense, walkable district like Miraflores. Beyond 1km, customers tend to drive/cab and the choice set widens to all of Lima.

gridDefinition.method: Street-radiating grid from Parque Kennedy (Miraflores' central plaza). Every named street within a 1km walk of Alcanfores 183 was walked virtually via Google Maps Street View and cross-referenced against Google Places, TripAdvisor, and Instagram location tags.

inclusionCriteria: Serves specialty coffee as a primary category (not just a bakery or restaurant that happens to serve coffee)
Located within ~1km walking distance of Alcanfores 183, OR a Lima-wide specialty leader included for benchmarking (clearly flagged as out-of-area)
Has a verifiable physical address or a confirmed operating location
Public-facing (Google Business Profile, TripAdvisor listing, Instagram location tag, or storefront signage visible on Street View)
exclusionCriteria: Chains with >10 Lima locations whose catchment is city-wide, not Miraflores-specific (Starbucks, Juan Valdez) — listed separately as context only
Bakeries and restaurants where coffee is clearly incidental to the core product (El Pan de la Chola included because coffee + bakery is central to its identity)
Closed businesses with no replacement operator in the same space (flagged in coverageLedger.excluded)
Vendors without a fixed physical address (e.g. coffee carts, market stalls)

competitors.name: Milenaria Cafe
competitors.googleReviewCountNote: Not directly verified; TripAdvisor shows 41 reviews. Google count likely higher.
competitors.positioning: Early-opening breakfast-and-coffee spot on the same street as Ursa; cozy, family-friendly, brunch-style menu.
strengths: Opens 6:30am — earliest opener on Alcanfores, captures pre-work market Ursa cannot reach (Ursa opens 7:30am)
Praised for pancakes, açaí bowls, oat-milk cappuccino — broad breakfast appeal
Cozy atmosphere per review consensus
Same-street location gives Milenaria strong walk-up visibility from Alcanfores foot traffic
weaknesses: Limited vegan options per reviews
Praised-for-pancakes identity is not a specialty-coffee identity; coffee is incidental to breakfast
'Not cheap' complaint theme — pricing friction
Not a roastery; buys roasted beans (no in-house roasting story)
competitors.ursaImplication: Milenaria is Ursa's nearest direct neighbor on Alcanfores and opens an hour earlier. Ursa should NOT try to out-breakfast Milenaria. Instead: position as the specialty-coffee destination on the same street, and use Milenaria's early-opener status as a referral partner (breakfast at Milenaria, espresso at Ursa) or extend hours selectively to 7am on Saturdays only. The same-street proximity is a feature, not a threat — Milenaria's customers walk past Ursa's door twice a day.

reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: Themes drawn from TripAdvisor reviews (n=41). Sample adequate for direction, not for coded frequency analysis.

competitors.googleReviewCountNote: Mentioned in travel forum; no verified Google Business Profile surfaced.
competitors.positioning: Mentioned in a travel forum as a coffee spot on Alcanfores near Vivanda supermarket. Limited online presence — may be a small or new operator, or may have closed/renamed.
strengths: Same-street proximity to Ursa (closest competitor by address if operating)
Forum mention suggests at least one loyal customer advocate
weaknesses: No verifiable Google Business Profile — discovery friction
No TripAdvisor presence found
Online footprint is near-zero — likely small/under-marketed or possibly closed
competitors.ursaImplication: If Coffee Notes is operating, it is Ursa's nearest competitor by address and shares the same Vivanda-anchored foot traffic. Ursa should physically verify Coffee Notes' status (walk-by) and, if operating, treat as a same-street reference point. If closed, the address is a cautionary tale about discoverability — Ursa's Google Business Profile investment (per REV-ENRICH) is the right antidote.

competitors.name: Estación 329
competitors.googleReviewCountNote: Not directly verified; TripAdvisor shows reviews.
competitors.tripAdvisorReviewCountNote: Rating verified; exact review count not captured at snapshot.
competitors.positioning: Cozy neighborhood cafe on the Palacios specialty-coffee corridor. Two-location operator (also Bolívar 153). Known for friendly service, exceptional coffee quality, and pastries.
strengths: Exceptional coffee quality per TripAdvisor (4.8★)
Friendly, kind service — repeatedly praised
Delicious pastries — food attachment
Two-location footprint gives operational scale without chain feel
Bolívar 153 second location extends catchment
weaknesses: Cozy = small; likely limited seating at peak
Lower online visibility than Neira/Punto on the same corridor
No clear roastery story (appears to be a brewer/operator, not a roaster)
competitors.ursaImplication: Estación 329 owns the 'cozy + kind + quality' position on Palacios — a position Ursa could match but should differentiate via roastery visibility. Their two-location scale is a cautionary tale: growth can dilute the single-site intimacy that makes Ursa ownable.

reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: TripAdvisor reviews; sample size small. No systematic complaints surfaced — direction only.

competitors.name: Neira Café Lab
competitors.positioning: Barista-champion-led specialty chain. Founded by Harrysson Neira (barista champion). 4+ Lima locations including a WorkCafé cobrand. Featured in Michelin guide. La Marzocco equipment. The most review-volume-rich competitor in the catchment.
strengths: Barista champion founder (Harrysson Neira) — credibility halo
911 Google reviews at 4.7★ — dominant review-volume position in catchment
4+ locations — operational scale and brand reach
Michelin guide feature — international recognition
La Marzocco equipment — visible quality signal
WorkCafé cobrand extends daypart coverage into remote-work
weaknesses: WorkCafé cobrand dilutes pure-café identity — customers may associate with co-working more than coffee
Chain scale erodes single-site intimacy
4+ locations means staff variance across sites — quality consistency risk
Premium pricing expected at champion-led shop
competitors.ursaImplication: Neira is the Goliath of the catchment: champion founder, 911 reviews, Michelin mention. Ursa must NOT out-scale Neira. Ursa's counter is single-site intimacy + the bear + two-bar theatre. Ursa's Aeropress champion (Paulo Sierra, per Instagram) is a direct credibility counter to Neira's champion founder — a fact-based, ownable response.

complaints: WorkCafé confusion (is it a cafe or a co-working space?)
reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: Themes inferred from 911 Google + 35 TripAdvisor reviews. Sample adequate for direction; specific complaint frequencies not coded.

competitors.name: Arabica Espresso Bar
competitors.googleReviewCountNote: Rating not directly verified at snapshot; described in editorial sources.
competitors.positioning: European-style espresso bar: tiny space, locals stopping in for latte/espresso, stand-up or quick-sit model. Concept is volume + speed, not lingering.
strengths: European espresso-bar format is differentiated in Miraflores (most competitors are sit-down cafes)
Tiny footprint = low rent, high throughput
Locals-oriented (not tourist-trap) — repeat customer base
Espresso purist positioning
weaknesses: Tiny space = no lingering, no remote-work daypart
Stand-up model limits audience to quick-stop customers
Lower review visibility — under-discovered
No roastery story visible
competitors.ursaImplication: Arabica owns the stand-up espresso-bar niche Ursa does NOT want. Ursa's two-bar theatre (espresso + coldbrew) explicitly invites lingering. The lesson: do not chase Arabica's speed/throughput model; defend the lingering-craft niche instead.

reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: Themes from editorial descriptions and forum mentions; review sample not directly coded.

competitors.name: Punto Café
competitors.googleReviewCountNote: Described as 'high' in research; exact rating not captured. TripAdvisor shows 5.0★ with 2 reviews.
competitors.positioning: Award-winning specialty roaster. CAM Café 2025 2nd place (Ursa was top-5). Premios Somos 2024 winner. Terrace overlooking San Martín park — view as a differentiator. In-house roasting.
strengths: CAM Café 2025 2nd place — direct head-to-head award recognition vs. Ursa's top-5
Premios Somos 2024 winner — mainstream Lima recognition
Terrace overlooking San Martín park — view-driven destination appeal
In-house roasting — specialty credibility
Established local recognition
weaknesses: Limited Art Nouveau / craft visual identity — generic 'specialty' aesthetic
TripAdvisor review count very low (n=2) despite awards — discovery gap on TripAdvisor
Award-driven positioning is brittle if awards fade
competitors.ursaImplication: Punto Café is Ursa's most direct head-to-head competitor: both in CAM 2025 top-5, both Miraflores, both roasters. Ursa's differentiators are: bear-led brand (Punto has no animal/character), two-bar theatre, named-drink portmanteaus. The award race with Punto is the single most measurable competitive benchmark — Ursa should track CAM results annually.

praise: terrace view over San Martín park
reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: TripAdvisor sample n=2 — too small for theme analysis. Themes drawn from editorial positioning.

competitors.name: Terrua Cafe
competitors.positioning: Farm-to-cup specialty roaster. Owns Villa Rica origin (Fundo San Josefa). Offers honey, washed, and natural process coffees. US$25 tasting flight is the signature premium experience. Quiet room, kind service, patio seating.
strengths: Farm-to-cup origin ownership (Villa Rica, Fundo San Josefa) — verifiable provenance story
US$25 tasting flight — premium experience pricing power
513 Google reviews at 4.6★ + 37 TripAdvisor at 5.0★ — strong dual-platform footprint
Process variety (honey, washed, natural) — education depth
Patio + quiet room = atmospheric differentiation
Kind service per reviews
weaknesses: US$25 flight ceiling limits frequency — premium-only positioning
Behind-Larco location less walk-up visible than Alcanfores/Palacios
Single origin (Villa Rica) is a strength AND a limitation — narrow terroir story vs. multi-origin roasters
competitors.ursaImplication: Terrua owns the premium-tasting-flight niche. Ursa's counter per existing strategy: tiered tastings — accessible entry (S/.25-35) plus premium depth (S/.60-90) vs. Terrua's flat US$25 ceiling. Ursa's Filtrado Lonya origin line is the multi-origin counter to Terrua's single-origin Villa Rica story.

reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: Themes from 513 Google + 37 TripAdvisor reviews. Sample adequate for direction.

competitors.name: Cate Tasting Room
competitors.positioning: Tasting-room format combining coffee and chocolate. Surquillo is the second location. Concept is guided tasting, not casual drop-in.
strengths: Coffee + chocolate crossover — differentiated experience vs. coffee-only competitors
190 Google reviews at 4.6★ — strong footprint
Tasting-room format supports premium pricing
Two locations (Miraflores + Surquillo) extend catchment
weaknesses: Tasting-room format may not capture casual walk-up coffee demand
Chocolate crossover dilutes pure-coffee identity
Less frequent visit model vs. daily-cafe competitors
competitors.ursaImplication: Cate validates the tasting-flight model Terrua also uses — there is demand for paid, guided tasting in Miraflores. Ursa's tiered-tasting counter (per Terrua implication) is reinforced. Ursa should NOT add chocolate — dilutes pure-coffee identity. Instead, deepen coffee-only tasting depth.

reviewThemes.sampleSizeNote: Themes from 190 Google + 17 TripAdvisor reviews; specific complaints not systematically surfaced.

competitors.name: Café Verde
competitors.googleReviewCountNote: Rating not captured at snapshot — status uncertain (see status).
competitors.statusNote: One source reports 'Permanently closed.' Cannot confirm operating status. Treat as possibly closed.
competitors.positioning: Sustainability-led roaster. Roasts own coffee. Green messaging as primary identity.
strengths: In-house roasting (if operating)
Sustainability narrative — values-driven customer appeal
Santa Cruz location on edge of catchment
weaknesses: POSSIBLY PERMANENTLY CLOSED — one source confirms closure
Generic sustainability messaging ('green' could be anyone's)
If closed, the Santa Cruz space is a cautionary tale about over-niche positioning
competitors.ursaImplication: If closed, Café Verde's failure is a lesson: generic 'sustainability' messaging is not a defensible position. Ursa's origin stories must be SPECIFIC (named farms, named producers, named lots) — not 'we are sustainable.' If operating, Ursa should differentiate via specificity (Filtrado Lonya, named lots) vs. Café Verde's generic green copy.

competitors.name: El Pan de la Chola
competitors.address: Av. Mariscal La Mar 1081, Miraflores (also Dasso location)
competitors.tripAdvisorReviewCountNote: Rating 4.3★ verified; exact count not captured. Dasso location rated 3.9★ on TripAdvisor.
competitors.positioning: Best-bakery-in-Lima per some reviews. Bakery-primary with coffee as attachment. Two locations (La Mar + Dasso). The bakery identity is stronger than the coffee identity.
strengths: Best-bakery-in-Lima recognition per editorial reviews
Two-location footprint (La Mar + Dasso)
TripAdvisor 4.3★ — strong mainstream recognition
Bakery + coffee crossover captures breakfast + brunch daypart
weaknesses: Bakery-primary identity means coffee is incidental — not a specialty-coffee competitor per se
Dasso location rated lower (3.9★) — quality variance across sites
Not a roaster; coffee is bought-in
Bakery queue model can be hostile to coffee-only quick stops
competitors.ursaImplication: El Pan de la Chola is a SUBSTITUTE, not a direct competitor — customers choosing between a bakery breakfast and a coffee stop. Ursa's positioning is orthogonal: not the best bakery, but the best coffee. Ursa could partner with El Pan de la Chola for pastry supply (complement, not compete) — a channel partnership opportunity.

competitors.name: Puku Puku
competitors.address: Multiple Miraflores locations (Larco, La Paz, Narciso)

competitors.positioning: Multi-location specialty chain. Owns the 'microlotes' (microlot) positioning. World's 100 Best Coffee Shops nominee. Retail bags at S/.49 — retail-channel reach. Multiple Lima + Miraflores locations.
strengths: 'Microlotes' positioning is ownable and resonant — single-word category claim
World's 100 Best Coffee Shops nominee — international recognition
Multi-location Miraflores footprint (Larco, La Paz, Narciso) — high catchment coverage
Retail bag channel (S/.49) — at-home consumption capture
658 TripAdvisor reviews across Miraflores locations — strong review footprint
weaknesses: Chain feel at scale — atmosphere erodes with location count

Ursa's counter: a microlot SUB-LINE (not the whole brand), wrapped in the bear + Art Nouveau identity. The retail-bag channel (S/.49) is a channel opportunity for Ursa — currently Ursa's retail reach is Instagram-only.

competitors.name: Amauta Coffee
competitors.positioning: Miraflores specialty operator with a small TripAdvisor footprint. 'Amauta' (Quechua for 'teacher/wise one') suggests an educational or heritage-led identity.
strengths: 'Amauta' (Quechua for teacher) — heritage-led naming, ownable linguistic identity
Operating with at least some TripAdvisor presence (n=7)
weaknesses: TripAdvisor 4.1★ is the lowest in the catchment among rated competitors — quality gap
Very small review sample (n=7) — low discovery
No clear champion/positioning beyond the name
competitors.ursaImplication: Amauta's heritage naming ('teacher' in Quechua) is the kind of specific, ownable linguistic identity Ursa should learn from — but Amauta's execution (4.1★ rating) is the cautionary tale. Identity without execution does not win. Ursa's bear + 'Un gramo a la vez' has both identity and (per reviews) execution.

competitors.name: Bisetti
competitors.positioning: Barranco-based specialty roaster. Owns the 'escuela de café' (coffee school) positioning — educational authority. Lima-wide benchmark competitor despite Barranco location.
strengths: Owns 'escuela de café' positioning — educational authority is a strong, defensible category claim
Barranco location captures the creative-district customer base
Coffee-school model supports premium pricing and brand depth
weaknesses: Educational focus can feel formal — 'homework' rather than 'third place'
Barranco location is outside Miraflores 1km catchment — not a walk-up competitor
School format may not capture casual coffee demand
competitors.ursaImplication: Bisetti owns the 'school' position. Ursa's counter per existing strategy: compete on education but make it warmer/experiential. Ursa's cupping + tasting format should feel like discovery, not lecture. Bisetti is a benchmark, not a walk-up competitor.

methodology.approach: Street-radiating virtual grid walk via Google Maps Street View, cross-referenced against Google Places API search results, TripAdvisor Miraflores listings, and Instagram location-tagged posts.
dataSources: Google Maps / Google Places (ratings, review counts, hours, status)
Editorial travel guides (Lima Gourmet Company, Wanderlog, Barista Magazine)
Forum mentions (Reddit, travel forums) for low-online-presence operators
CAM Café Perú 2025 competition results (award verification)
World's 100 Best Coffee Shops nominee list (Puku Puku)
limitations: Distances are walking-distance estimates from Google Maps, not surveyed measurements. Accuracy ±50m.
Google ratings and review counts are point-in-time snapshots (2026-08-01); they fluctuate daily.
Three operators (Coffee Notes, Café Verde, OK Café) have uncertain status and require physical walk-by verification.
Café Verde may be permanently closed; one source reports closure but conflicting evidence was not resolved at snapshot.
Review themes are inferred from review text and editorial summaries; coded theme frequency analysis was NOT performed (sample sizes too small for most competitors).
Same-street proximity to Ursa (Milenaria, Coffee Notes) is address-based; actual storefront visibility and foot-flow overlap require on-site verification.
The census captures named, public-facing competitors. Informal/unnamed coffee vendors (carts, market stalls) are excluded by design.
nextSteps: Physical walk-by verification of Coffee Notes, Café Verde, and OK Café status (30-day priority)
Coded theme-frequency analysis on the 3 highest-volume competitors (Neira 911, Terrua 513, Puku Puku 658) to convert themes into quantitative signals
Quarterly re-verification of competitor status (open/closed/new openings) per unresolved-uncertainties.md
Annual tracking of CAM Café competition results as the most measurable competitive benchmark
